--- title: "[GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Gradient-boosted survival model minimizing the Cox partial-likelihood loss. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_boosting.py#L198-L486){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis( *, n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3, min_samples_leaf=3, subsample=1.0, max_features=None, random_state=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Builds an additive risk score by sequentially fitting shallow squared-error regression trees to the negative gradient of the negative Cox partial log-likelihood (the martingale residuals under the current model) and adding a shrunken version of each tree. The result is a flexible, non-linear generalization of the Cox model: strong predictive performance on structured tabular data, without a global proportional-hazards assumption on individual covariates. A Breslow baseline hazard turns the additive log-risk score into per-subject survival and cumulative-hazard functions. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_estimators]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of boosting iterations (trees). [learning_rate]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Shrinkage applied to each tree's contribution. Smaller values need more trees but generalize better. [max_depth]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum depth of each regression tree (interaction depth). [min_samples_leaf]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum number of samples in each leaf of a tree. [subsample]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fraction of the training rows sampled (without replacement) to grow each tree. Values below `1.0` give stochastic gradient boosting. [max_features]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates considered per split: `None` (all, default), `"sqrt"`, `"log2"`, an int, or a float fraction. [random_state]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Seed or `numpy.random.Generator` for subsampling and per-node feature selection. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a gradient-boosted survival model on the bundled `lung` dataset: ::: {#1001290e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="pandas").dropna(subset=["ph.ecog", "ph.karno"]) # Fit the model and score the first five subjects gbm = gw.GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis( n_estimators=200, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=2, random_state=0 ).fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog + ph.karno + wt.loss", data=lung) gbm.predict(lung)[:5] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` array([0.63006698, 1.09057783, 0.59369757, 1.18981321, 0.58051085]) ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the gradient-boosted survival model to a right-censored response.
predict() Predict a risk score, linear predictor, or survival / cumulative-hazard curves.
variable_importance() Impurity-based variable importance (normalized total squared-error reduction).
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the gradient-boosted survival model to a right-censored response. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_boosting.py#L285-L408){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(surv, covariates=None, *, data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response, built with `gw.Surv(time=..., event=...)`. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side sets `covariates`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe, a 2-D array, or a right-hand-side formula string evaluated against `data`. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `covariates`. When `surv`{.gd-no-link} is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [self]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator, with cached attributes including `trees_`, `event_times_`, `feature_importances_`, `n_features_in_`, and `feature_names_in_`. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a gradient-boosted model on the `lung` dataset and inspect the feature importances. Importances are normalized so they sum to one: ::: {#24747ccf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="pandas").dropna( subset=["ph.ecog", "ph.karno"] ) gbm = gw.GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis( n_estimators=200, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=2, random_state=0 ).fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog + ph.karno + wt.loss", data=lung) gbm ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis (200 trees, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=2) n = 213, events = 151, features = 5 (13 observations deleted due to missingness) ``` ::: ::: The formula interface works the same way: ::: {#113d30dc .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} gbm2 = gw.GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis( n_estimators=100, random_state=0 ).fit( "Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex + ph.ecog + ph.karno", data=lung, ) gbm2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` GradientBoostingSurvivalAnalysis (100 trees, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3) n = 226, events = 163, features = 4 ``` ::: ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict a risk score, linear predictor, or survival / cumulative-hazard curves. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_boosting.py#L416-L473){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(newdata=None, *, type="risk", times=None, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} 1. `type="risk"` (default): the relative hazard $\exp(F(x))$, a 1-D array where higher values indicate higher risk. 2. `type="lp"`: the additive log-risk score $F(x)$ (the boosted Cox linear predictor). 3. `type="survival"`: survival $S(t \mid x) = \exp(-H_0(t)\,e^{F(x)})$ at `times`. 4. `type="cumulative_hazard"`: $H(t \mid x) = H_0(t)\,e^{F(x)}$ at `times`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates to predict for. `None` predicts for the training subjects. A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["risk"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : One of `"risk"`, `"lp"`, `"survival"`, or `"cumulative_hazard"`. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Times at which to evaluate curves. Defaults to the training event times. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : DataFrame backend for curve output. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray or DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A risk / linear-predictor vector, or a curve frame with a `time` column and one column per subject. ::: ### [variable_importance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Impurity-based variable importance (normalized total squared-error reduction). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_boosting.py#L475-L486){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python variable_importance(*, format=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each split's reduction in squared error is credited to its covariate and summed across all trees, then normalized to sum to one. Returns a table sorted by importance. :::
